long_biography.plain_text:
Buying Lucasfilm's computer-graphics division in 1986 gave Steve Jobs a second entrepreneurial platform. He financed the company that became Pixar, remained its controlling shareholder and took it public after Toy Story. Disney's all-stock acquisition in 2006 converted that holding into the largest part of his personal fortune and placed him on Disney's board.

At Apple, Jobs paired product strategy with tight control of hardware, software and industrial design. After returning, he narrowed the product line and oversaw a sequence that moved from the iMac and iPod to the iPhone and iPad. Those products rebuilt Apple around integrated consumer devices and digital services.
long_biography.html:
Buying Lucasfilm's computer-graphics division in 1986 gave Steve Jobs a second entrepreneurial platform. He financed the company that became Pixar, remained its controlling shareholder and took it public after Toy Story. Disney's all-stock acquisition in 2006 converted that holding into the largest part of his personal fortune and placed him on Disney's board.

At Apple, Jobs paired product strategy with tight control of hardware, software and industrial design. After returning, he narrowed the product line and oversaw a sequence that moved from the iMac and iPod to the iPhone and iPad. Those products rebuilt Apple around integrated consumer devices and digital services.
